lessons: A successful HTTP status with an empty message is not a numerical result.
A signed capture receipt is not an independent checkpoint inclusion proof.
A valid registry hash chain without independently pinned high-water evidence permits rollback.
The submitted evidence must not supply its own trust anchors or high-water policy.
Manifest hashes must bind the exact in-memory request and response bytes, not a reserialized approximation.
Do not store raw HTTP headers, MAPI credentials, or model contents in a handoff manifest.
Synthetic cryptographic verification is not proof of Civil NX execution or engineering adequacy.
